title: Choose the poster's world
question: The shared poster gets its own look (the modal stays Ritmo Vivo). The roll assigned Clave Count Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Clave Count Sheet
options.lineage: the dancer's 8-count and the 3-2 clave pattern, printed as notation
options.thesis: Every night is set on the count every salsero knows by heart: 1-2-3 · 5-6-7 ·. The pauses on 4 and 8 hold the facts.
options.viewport: Story 9:16: a rose field split by one 8-count bar. Giant numerals 1 2 3 · 5 6 7 · run down the sheet; the 3-2 clave hits sit as black dots over their counts. The title is set across counts 1-3, the date lands on the 4 pause, the venue and time on the 8 pause, and the QR plus the short link close the bar. The 4:5 feed cut folds the same bar into two rows of four.
options.risk: Numerals can overpower the title if the count isn't clearly just the structure. Bachata's 1-2-3-tap needs its own variant of the bar, or the sheet only rings true for salsa.

raised.raise: Every fact gets a leader line down to its count, so the sheet reads like an annotated promoter flyer, not a chart.
Hierarchy comes from scale alone: one enormous numeral size, one title size, one fact size. No boxes, no chips.
The count line is the only shared order; the eye follows it the way you'd follow a river of lanterns.
In the modal preview the count plays through once (1 to 8, the clave hits landing on beat) before it settles.
Times and prices use tabular figures pinned to the grid, so every poster lines up with the next.

options.label: Fania Sleeve
options.lineage: 1970s Fania Records album covers (Izzy Sanabria-era hand lettering)
options.thesis: Every night pressed as its own salsa LP: title lettered like a record name, venue and date as the track list.
options.viewport: A square LP sleeve centred in the 9:16 story, flyer art as the cover photo, title in fat hand-drawn caps. The back-cover strip below lists date, time, venue, price and QR as a track list.
options.risk: The most familiar reading of 'salsa poster', and it repeats the vinyl record the homepage hero already uses.

options.label: Promoter Flyer Density
options.lineage: street-fashion magazine spreads, fused with Latin club promoter flyers
options.thesis: The flyer packed to the edges: cut-out dancers, outlined headline, every fact called out by hand.
options.viewport: The flyer image cut out and shingled, headline outlined three times, price and time on hand-drawn call-outs, QR in a starburst.
options.case: Holds audience identification (it looks like the flyers dancers already repost) but loses on clarity: time and venue get buried in the density.
options.risk: Needs real cut-out photography for every event; flyerless events collapse.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: The night's name as the specimen: one enormous word, the facts as tiny specimen labels.
options.viewport: The title fills the story at glyph scale; date, venue, price and QR sit as a small label row at the foot.
options.case: Holds clarity (the facts are crisp) but loses audience identification: it reads as a design studio, not a dance night.
options.risk: Long titles break the specimen scale.

options.label: Night-Market Sign River
options.case: Fuses poorly: dancers don't identify with market wayfinding, and a single event doesn't need a route.
options.kept: One continuous line that orders the whole reading.

options.label: Glaze River Shelf
options.case: Fuses poorly on both axes: nothing in a dance night maps to glaze behaviour.
options.kept: One accent colour reserved for one meaning.

options.label: Paper Automata
options.case: Fuses poorly: charming, but a static shared image can't carry the crank motion.
options.kept: One timeline drives the motion, played once in the preview.

options.label: Collider Event Display
options.case: Fuses poorly: technical spectacle with no link to the dance floor.
options.kept: Tabular figures pinned to a grid.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The event-story template: flyer art full-bleed, gradient scrim, title and details at the bottom.
canonCard.viewport: The flyer fills the story; title, date, venue, price, QR and link sit on a dark scrim in the lower third.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other event story in the feed.
